missions.title: A key handover
paragraphs: A contractor needs access to a shared room. Nobody is clearly responsible for providing the key. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

On this occasion, we decide to name one person to manage access. The expected benefit is that the contractor can reach the room at the agreed time. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

The aim is to make the next step easier to understand and carry out. A short message confirming the arrangement can reduce the chance of different assumptions. If the outcome is less useful than expected, the explanation and the plan can be revised.

When arranging work at home, a clear description helps the person prepare. Explain what is not working, when the problem started, and whether anything has already been tried. Before the visit, check the likely cost and who needs to be there. Afterwards, ask how to use or maintain anything that has been repaired.
In a similar conversation, you could say: “What time should I expect you tomorrow morning?” “How much will it cost, including the new part?” “Is there anything I need to do before you arrive?”
